title: Size deep in-the-money calls by exposure, not by share count
summary: Size deep in-the-money calls by the exposure you want, not like stock. Pick the dollar exposure, for example $100,000. Compute option leverage: delta x stock price / option price (about 1.35 in the example). Buy only enough contracts to match it. Dollar P&L then matches the stock, percent P&L differs, and you avoid more than 100% exposure by accident.

steps.caption: We want $100,000 of exposure to a $100 stock: 1,000 shares.
Ten deep ITM calls with delta near 1 give about the same exposure for much less capital.
The dollar P&L of the two lines is close. The percent P&L differs because the calls use less capital.
Sizing the calls like stock (spending $100,000 on calls) would give many times the intended exposure.

takeaways: Decide your dollar exposure first, then size the option to it.
Option leverage = delta x stock price / option price.
Matched exposure gives the same dollar P&L as stock but a different percent P&L.
Sizing deep ITM calls like stock can push you above 100% portfolio exposure without noticing.
caveats: The transcript's numeric example is partly garbled (about 1.35 leverage with a $70 option); the chart uses round illustrative numbers.
